newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LIFFE robusta rally seen, Vietnam news a dampener.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE robusta rally seen, Vietnam news a dampener.

text.p: Vietnam's announcement it cannot afford to join the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) may dampen an expected rally in LIFFE robusta futures prices later on Tuesday, Southeast Asian traders said.

But any sign of profit-taking is likely to be limited by news Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop is forecast to reach only 18-20 million 60-kg bags, versus 25 million in 1996/97, and also a bullish overnight close on CSCE coffee futures in New York.
"This may deflate the market," a senior trader, responding to the Vietnam news, told Reuters. "It may encourage some of those who have taken long positions to liquidate their holdings," he said.
"The market may reverse itself on this development," another trader said. "But there are bullish technical factors present in the market to stem any sharp fall."
Vietnam said on Tuesday it is considering joining the ACPC, but cannot afford to do so at present.

ACPC chairman, Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze, said at a special association meeting in Rio de Janeiro on Monday that Vietnam was considering joining the ACPC after he held an earlier meeting in Hanoi with the country's vice-minister of Foreign Affairs.
Gauze's comments sparked a rally in LIFFE robusta future priceson Monday and the most active May contract rose $53 yesterday to end at $1,380 a tonne. March rose $33 to also close at $1,380.

One trader predicted that LIFFE robusta futures may well ignore the news on Vietnam until the ACPC meeting on an export reduction plan proposed by African countries concludes in Rio de Janeiro on Friday.
"We could easily be trading at $1,500," the trader said.
One chartist cautioned, however, that any rise would be vulnerable to long liquidation: "At that level ($1,500), we may see profit-taking hitting the market."

One regional coffee analyst said that even if Hanoi wanted to accomodate the Africans and join the ACPC, Vietnam does not have the resources to finance the storage of coffee as part of a retention plan.
"The will and desire to join is there. But storing and financing requires a lot of logistics. I don't see the (Vietnamese) government being in a position to do either," the analyst said.
